steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The subjunctive mood expresses possibility, purpose, wish, or subordinate action — unlike the indicative, which states facts. | Key Fact: Present subjunctive is formed by changing the stem vowel: 1st conjugation changes -a- to -e- (muset), 2nd changes -e- to -ea- (moneas), 3rd/4th change to -a- (ducamus, audiamus). | Key Fact: Imperfect subjunctive is formed by adding -re to the infinitive: laudarem (I would praise / I might praise). | Key Fact: Purpose clauses: ut + subjunctive = 'in order to' (positive); ne + subjunctive = 'in order not to' (negative). Example: venit ut pater videret (he came in order that his father might see).
